rows.title: Cooking with Maths

intro_text.eng:
Cooking can help your child start learning maths!
💚 Invite your child to help you cook for your family, or to choose something they would like to cook

steps_text.eng:
🍅 Ask your child to count different ingredients. Help them if it’s difficult!

🔟 Help your child to understand adding and subtracting quantities 

📝 Encourage your child to recognise numbers on packaging

 👀 Ask your child about the different sizes of ingredients - e.g. which is bigger/biggest?

tips_text.eng: 🔄 Think about when you will cook together again! You can also practise understanding numbers and quantities during other activities like shopping or building/making things

rows.title: Following Instructions

intro_text.eng:
👂 Play a game in which your child listens to and tries to remember strings of instructions.
This will be useful in school, at home, and later in life!

steps_text.eng:
Start with just one instruction using an object in your home. For example “touch the red ball” 🔴

Slowly add more instructions (e.g “then pick up the cup ☕), but tell your child that they can only start once you’ve finished giving the instructions.
See how many your child can follow without forgetting!

🔄 Now swap roles! It’s your child’s turn to give you instructions! They can use the same objects if they want.
You can also try this game with a group of children! Make sure they take turns :)

rows.title: One-on-One Time

intro_text.eng: 💚 Spending time just with your child and taking an interest in them can improve your relationship

steps_text.eng:
👀 When you child is playing alone or occupying themselves quietly, join them and show interest in what they are doing

👂Ask questions about their activity, and listen to them

Let your child lead the activity, follow them to build their confidence and autonomy 😃

👀 Say what you see - describing everything and supporting your child’s actions

tips_text.eng: Be positive, praise your child, and enjoy spending this time with them 😃💚

rows.title: Playtime with Books

intro_text.eng: 📖 Book sharing will help your child learn and is a fun, playful activity to spend quality time together

steps_text.eng:
⏰ Choose a time when you won’t be disturbed, and try to stop any distractions - e.g. turn off the TV and put away phones

📖 If your child wants to choose a book, that’s fine, otherwise choose for them

💚 Sit close together and follow your child attention and lead 
Point at things, name and repeat words. Help your child learn more about what interests them in the book 👀 
If there are words or numbers in the book, ask and help your child recognise letters numbers, and simple words 💡 

Link things in the books to your child life, and use words about emotions and talk about them! 😃

tips_text.eng:
🔄 If possible, start a regular routine to read together when your child isn’t too tired or hungry
Reading together is one of the best ways to help your child learn and prepare for success in school! 🎓

rows.title: I Spy!

intro_text.eng: 👀 I spy is a fun game to play with your child that will help them learn about letters and words!

steps_text.eng:
Choose an object or a thing around you, and don’t tell your child what it is. It should be something that your child knows the word for. For example “ball” ⚽

👀 Then say “I spy with my little eye, something beginning with *and then say the first letter of the word* which in this case is “b”

Your child should look around and guess what the object is. When they guess it right, praise them and swap roles! If they can’t get it, give them some clues, like “it’s round” or “it’s black and white”. ✅

tips_text.eng: Play this game with as many objects as possible and as many different letters! Help your child to learn about the different letters and sounds in words. This will help them learn to read at home and school. 🎓

rows.title: Categorising and Organising

intro_text.eng:
Help your child to learn by sorting objects and things! 🔵🔷

Your child will learn by understanding how things fit and group together (eg, bear = animal, mango = fruit, blue = colour) 🧸

steps_text.eng:
Find a book with different pictures and help your child to find things in a particular category (e.g. “Find all of the animals”) 👀

Find safe objects in the house, get your child to group them by colour, size, or types of object (cups, plates). Then make more complicated categories (e.g. small cups, big cups) ☕

tips_text.eng: 🔄 You can play the categorising game anywhere! Just look around and ask your child to find things from the category you say!

rows.title: What Letter is This?

intro_text.eng: Playing games with letters can help your child learn the alphabet and how letters are put together to make words.

steps_text.eng:
📝 Write a letter on a piece of card or paper (e.g. “p”)

👂 Say the letter out loud and ask your child to say it too!

Ask your child to say some words that begin with the letter “p”, give them clues like “What starts with “p”? Plant… what else? 🌱

👀 Ask your child to look for objects in your house that begin with a letter (eg “p” for plate). Help them find things.

🔄 Try a new letter every day!

rows.title: Riddles Help Children Learn

intro_text.eng: Riddles and puzzles are a fun way to build thinking skills! 💡

steps_text.eng:
Do you remember any riddles from your childhood? If you can’t then make one up, they can be very simple! 😃
Like “What can you see at night but not in the day” Answer: “The moon” 🌙

If your child is finding them difficult, try an easy one like: “What is round, bouncy and can be thrown or kicked?” Answer: “A ball” ⚽

Your child can also try making riddles! 💡

You can have fun with riddles anywhere at any time - like travelling on a bus or in a car 🚗

rows.title: What's New?

intro_text.eng: Learning is fun! 🎓

steps_text.eng:
❓ Ask your child to think of a new, fun skill you could learn together. 
For example: keeping a ball in the air with your foot, juggling, making soup, moonwalking, whistling, saying the alphabet backwards, learning all the states in Malaysia. 

🔄 Take turns trying out the new skill. Make sure to praise each other and learn and play together!

😃 Once you have mastered the skill, choose another skill to learn together.

tips_text.eng: 💛 Approach learning the skill in a kind and fun way, and do not judge your child or yourself for your ability in the skill.

rows.title: Make up a Story

intro_text.eng: Creating stories together is a great way to have fun with imagination - and to build your child’s creativity! 📖

steps_text.eng:
5️⃣ With your child, come up with 5 words to use. They can be any words you want! For example: banana, spaceship, fish, water, painting, cooking, wedding. If you need to remember them, write them clearly on a paper with your child.

🎂 Start your story with, “Once upon a time, there was a…” and use one of the words from the list in the first part. For example, “Once upon a time, there was a family who worked on a *banana* farm.”

📝 Let your child make up the next part using another word from the list.

🔄 Take turns until you have used all the words and created a story. 

🎁 Ask your child what their favourite part of the story was, and tell them yours!

tips_text.eng: 🔔 Be creative and do not tell your child what to say. It does not need to be a real story to be fun!

rows.title: Playing with Vegetables

intro_text.eng: 🌱 Help your child learn by thinking and talking about vegetables!

steps_text.eng:
🍅 Mix together 2-3 different ingredients of your choice (like onions, tomatoes and corn example). Say: “Help me sort these vegetables into piles?” Try sorting them by size.

😃 Remind me!
Talk about your child’s experiences. Ask questions and wait for answers. Follow your child’s interest. 
“Can you help me remember what is at the market?” “Do they sell carrots at the market?” “Do the sell anything yellow at the market?” “What else do they sell?” “Can you think of other things they sell?”

💡Can you think of something similar?
Say: We are going to think of some things that are similar or different from what I tell you. So listen carefully!”
Here is a tomato. Can you think of something else that is red like a tomato? 🍅
Can you think something else that is round like a tomato? ⚽

intro_text.eng: Get ready to explore animals with your child! 🧸

steps_text.eng:
🧸 Active animals: Take turns with your child doing animal actions: Hop like a frog, stretch like a cat, run like a dog, slither like a snake, flap like a bird

💡All the animals we can think of - think about groups of animals!
What are all the animals we can think of that have feathers?
What are all the animals we can think of that eat plants? 🌱
What are all the animals we can think of that lay eggs?

😃 Counting rabbits
🔟 Find 10 rocks and put them in a line, tell your child that they are rabbits!
Ask your child to count the rabbits!
Put the rabbits into 2 equal piles. Ask your child to give you 3 rabbits. Say “If you give me 3, how many rabbits do you have”

rows.title: Active Counting

intro_text.eng: 👋 Clap, hop, jump: Play the following game with your child. Make it active!

steps_text.eng:
1️⃣ Clap hands 1 time. 2️⃣ Clap hands 2 times.
1️⃣ Jump 1 time. 2️⃣ Jump 2 times.
1️⃣ Hop 1 time.
3️⃣ Hop 3 times.
💡Can you hop, then jump, then clap? 
🏆 Can you clap twice, jump once, and hop three times?

tips_text.eng:
💡Remembering Instructions
Take turns playing a game where you give 2-3 instructions that the other person has to remember to follow. Make sure physical movement is included!
For example:
Hop twice, turn around.
Jump to the kitchen, pick up a spoon, then run back. ✅

rows.title: Thinking Games

intro_text.eng: ❗ Mama/Daddy says!

steps_text.eng:
Play this game of giving instructions:
Mama/daddy says touch your head. Mama/daddy says open your mouth. Mama/daddy says turn around. Mama/daddy says touch your knees. Mama/daddy says jump twice. Mama/daddy says jump, then clap and sit.

👂 Go and stop: Play the game with your child
Say: When I say “stop”, we freeze. When I say “go”, we can walk again.
Once your child is familiar with the game, your child will lead.

🔵 🔴Blue-Red - now play this game!
If I say touch something blue, you need to touch something red. If I say touch something red, you need to touch something blue.

👀 Can you point to it?
Using a book or a magazine, or anything with pictures, say:
I am going to describe something on the page and you need to guess what it is and point to it. For example, “I see something that is [green and moves slowly].
Can you guess what it is?” 💚

👀 Show your child pictures in the book. Ask your child what is happening in the pictures and what happens next.

intro_text.eng: 📝 Have fun being creative with writing!

steps_text.eng:
You and your child can have fun writing with a pencil and paper, or with a stick and the sand!

Show them the simple things that you write - like shopping lists! Show them the words and each of the letters. Let them try to copy the words! 📖

rows.title: A Friendly Chat

intro_text.eng:
Talk to your child about something that they are interested in! 😃

💚 Spending quality time with your child and talking to them every day is a good way to develop a strong relationship.

steps_text.eng:
⚽ An easy way to start talking to your child is to ask them about something they are interested in, for example you could talk about topics such as: sports, books, movies, friends, music, celebrities, or school.

👂 You may not find everything your child shares to be interesting, but it’s important to show enthusiasm and an eagerness to learn.

rows.title: Get Active

intro_text.eng: Exercise is a great way to spend time together and it is so good for your health. 🌱

steps_text.eng:
Find a sport or exercise that both you and your child want to do and try it out together! 

⏰ Even walking for 10 minutes a day is good for you. 

⚽ Together you can walk, run, play soccer, swim, dance, or do any other sport.

🏆 Together, think of ways to make it even more fun. Can you jog to a certain point? Take turns being the coach? Can there be a small, free reward, like getting to decide the next activity?

🌈 Exercise becomes easier and more enjoyable the more you do it. 

🔄 If you or your child do not like the first exercise you pick, try a new exercise.

intro_text.eng: This fun game helps your toddler learn about their body.

steps_text.eng:
Use a big piece of paper (or cardboard) and help them lie down. Trace around their body with a pencil.

🌱 The benefits of this activity include improving body awareness, expanding vocabulary, and developing fine motor skills.

rows.title: Can you catch it?

intro_text.eng: Let’s see if you can follow instructions while catching a ball, or even a rolled-up pair of socks! This game will train your concentration and coordination. You can adjust the rules to make it perfect for every age!

steps_text.eng:
👫 Stand a few meters apart and gently toss the ball to each other. After a few throws, add rules!
⚽ When the thrower shouts ‘one’, the catcher has to catch the ball with their right hand and put their left foot out. If the thrower shouts ‘two’, the catcher catches with their left hand and puts their right foot out.
😊 Once you’re confident, add some extra rules! If the thrower shouts ‘three’, the catcher has to catch with their right hand and put their right foot out. And if the thrower shouts ‘four’, the catcher catches with their left hand and puts their left foot out.

For the game to work, make sure the number is called before you throw the ball, so the catcher has time to react!

💬 While playing, talk about your ideas: How are you working together? What’s working and what’s not?

🌟 Flip the Blanket is a fun way to build teamwork, creative thinking, problem-solving, and perseverance!

intro_text.eng:
Get ready to turn a picture into a fun jigsaw puzzle that boosts memory and direction skills! 🎨

steps_text.eng:

rows.title: Superhero Costume Raffle

intro_text.eng: You can transform into superheroes with this fun and imaginative dressing-up game! 👑

steps_text.eng:
2️⃣ Here’s what you’ll need: Two items of clothing for each person playing, and a pillowcase or bag to hold them.

🎁 Start by placing all the clothes in the pillowcase. 

👀 Hand the pillowcase to the smallest player first. Make sure their eyes are shut, then let them pull out one item of clothing. 

🔄 Next, pass the case around until everyone gets two items of clothing. 

✨ Now, everyone takes turns to imagine what superpower their pieces of clothing give them. Maybe a scarf makes you fly, or a hat gives you super speed - it’s totally up to your imagination!

🚗 Now it’s time to play! Put on your superpower clothes and act out a story together, like saving the world from a monster.

rows.title: Hot or cold

intro_text.eng: Ready to hunt for hidden treasure using clues? 🎁

steps_text.eng:
⚽ Here’s what you’ll need: something easy to hide, like toys or balls. 

👀 One player hides an object, while the others close their eyes. The player who hid the object will now give clues to help the others find it. 

☀️ When the person searching is getting close to where the object is hidden, the hider can say “getting warm!” or “hot!”, and when the searcher is going in the wrong direction, the hider can say “getting colder…”.

🔄 Take turns hiding objects and giving clues - it’s fun for everyone to get involved!

💡 For an extra challenge, hide multiple objects around the house and create a treasure map.

rows.title: Create Silly Characters

intro_text.eng: This game builds creativity, nurtures imagination, and helps teach kids to collaborate – while having lots of laughs! 🌈

steps_text.eng:
🎨 All you need to play this game is a piece of paper and a pen or pencil.

1️⃣ The first person draws the top (head, hat, hair) of a character. This can be as serious or silly as you want it to be.

🔄 Fold the drawing to cover up what has been drawn but leave two lines to show where the next person who is drawing should pick up.

2️⃣ Pass the paper on to the next person, who, without seeing what has already been drawn, will contribute the next set of features to the character: The shoulders or tummy. Fold the paper back to cover up the image and pass it on.

📝 Repeat until someone has drawn the feet of the character and then open your drawing up to see the masterpiece you have created together!

rows.title: Tricky Tower

intro_text.eng: Here is an exciting activity that will test your child’s ability to estimate risks, work as a team, and think creatively - all while having fun and developing fine motor skills ⭐

steps_text.eng:
🔶 Start by giving your child building blocks or something else they can stack. 

👋 Ask them to build a tower by stacking the blocks, using just one hand. This challenge helps build focus and concentration as they balance the blocks carefully.

⬆️ If other children or adults are around, you can make it into a match to see who can build the tallest tower the fastest.

🔄 Make the game even more challenging by asking your child to using their non-dominant hand. They’ll have to balance their wish to build the tallest tower with the risk of the tower collapsing.

rows.title: Unseen Guesses

intro_text.eng:
You can do this activity when you are together with at least three people in total. 3️⃣  

This game is not only fun but also helps children develop strong communication skills and teaches them how to work together to achieve a goal. 💚

steps_text.eng:
👀 Ask your child and another child/adult to sit next to each other. Blindfold both using a scarf or hat. 

🚗 Give your child an object and ask them to feel it and describe it, without saying the name of the object!

🎁 The other person’s job is to figure out what the object is based on the description. 

✅ The “guesser” can ask questions, but the “speaker” can only answer with "yes" or "no".

🔄 After each round, swap roles and play again, giving everyone a chance to be the “speaker” and “guesser” and the one to provides the object.

rows.title: Emotion Cards

intro_text.eng: Create cards of the main six emotions with Your Child: happy, sad, angry, disgusted, surprised, afraid 😃😔😣

steps_text.eng:
🔶 Draw, cut-out pictures from magazines, or take photos of family members showing different emotions. 

📝 Label each emotion and describe how each family member feels those emotions. 

🚩 Put the cards in a spot everyone agrees on, and use it throughout the day to name how everyone is feeling. For example, after school, everyone can point out the emotion they are experiencing. 

💡 This can help everyone in the family become experts in understanding themselves and be aware of what their bodies need! 💛
